## Scope and use

The core corpus includes work on intermediate computation that substitutes for, compresses, internalizes, or changes the schedule of an explicit reasoning trace. Architectural context that does not itself study implicit chain-of-thought is kept in a separate precursor collection. Coverage is curated and broad, not claimed to be exhaustive.

Use original papers as the authority for scientific claims. Facets and one-sentence summaries are editorial annotations. Every core record includes a canonical scholarly URL, ordered author_names, a stable record_url, and discovery provenance. first_public dates the earliest public version verified during curation, usually using the arXiv v1 submission date; it is not a verified public-announcement timestamp. citation_date is the preprint's initial arXiv submission date. Citation exports describe arXiv preprints, not later proceedings, and source URLs are not version-pinned. Related terms in the ontology are not necessarily synonyms.

Across the literature, related work may be labeled latent chain-of-thought, latent reasoning, continuous thought, hidden-state reasoning, or recurrent reasoning. This guide uses implicit chain-of-thought as the umbrella term while preserving each paper's terminology.

## Acknowledgment

Initial discovery and reconciliation draw substantially on the independently maintained [Awesome-Latent-CoT bibliography](https://github.com/EIT-NLP/Awesome-Latent-CoT) and its associated survey. The corpus is checked and maintained separately against primary scholarly sources.
